added_failures_note: Derived with reckon.crew.review.added_failures_from_gate_logs over the two gate logs the reviewed manifest itself cites for its affected arm: logs/base-arm-affected.log (revision f0cbdd0b4e, scratch tree base-f0cbdd0b4, 46 failed / 1003 passed / 1 skipped, EXIT=1) and logs/head-affected-arm-job.log (revision d882fadb63, 24 failed / 1026 passed) with no EXIT= line in the head log (see the separate finding) but a complete pytest summary. Both ids fail at head and are absent from the base log, so the count is a measured 2, not an unmeasured zero. The reviewed run's manifest carries no baseline_suite or after_suite JSON fields, so the named-file gate pair was checked too: logs/baseline-crew-recovery.log records 19 failed / 67 passed EXIT=1 at f0cbdd0b4e and logs/gate-all-debug-merged.log records 86 passed EXIT=0 at d882fadb63 (all_debug job 1319079), a delta of 19 removed and 0 added. The two added ids above come from the arm population the done_when names, and the manifest reports neither.

findings.text: The affected arm the reviewed done_when names does not show what the manifest implies: logs/base-arm-affected.log at f0cbdd0b4e reports 46 failed and 1003 passed, while this merged-head arm at d882fadb63 reports 24 failed and 1026 passed, and reckon.crew.review.added_failures_from_gate_logs over the two logs returns 2 ids present only at head - tests/test_promotion_beat_carries_fleet_state.py::test_promotion_carries_a_bounded_fleet_reading_without_changing_the_ledger (line 2057) and tests/test_promotion_beat_carries_fleet_state.py::test_an_unavailable_fleet_reading_does_not_block_promotion (line 2257). The manifest's landing line (manifest.md:11) states only the named-file gate and its test_logs line (manifest.md:13) cites both arm logs without the count or an attribution, so the done_when clause 'adds no failure against the base' is contradicted by the run's own cited evidence and never reported. The diff of both failures is a ledger-row shape (missing budget/execution_fit/gate_check keys, extra lineage/local/node keys) from the origin/main merge, not from the two files this node changed, but that attribution is the reviewer's inference: the node recorded none, and its pre-merge affected arm at f2c7aada3e (head-arm-affected-final.log) never ran to a summary line, so no pre-merge arm exists to separate the node's change from the merge.

The head affected arm's log ends at pytest's '24 failed, 1026 passed' summary with no EXIT= line, because logs/head-affected-arm.sh:5 runs 'set -eu' and the failing pytest aborts the script before its EXIT echo at line 15; the receipt therefore carries no readable status for the arm it is cited as, even though the runner's own summary names 24 failures.

The new 'isinstance(record.get("budget"), Mapping)' clause is a behaviour change to _stranded_launch as well as a new arm of _spawn_evidence: a pre-spawn pointer carrying a folded budget but no pid, worker record, stream or launch log was a stranded launch before this commit and is not one now. No test writes a pointer budget (grep for '"budget":' over tests/test_crew_recovery.py and the recovery tests finds only node time_budget fixtures), so reverting just this clause leaves the 86 named-file tests green; _stranded_launch's docstring at line 759 still lists only 'a worker record, a stream, or a launch log' as the evidence, understating the predicate it now calls.
